title: The 133.61 ms real-deck opened-transaction shape-text edit is six whole-slide MCE rewrites, not the revision proof
decision: retained, attribution and frozen design; nothing implemented
code_state: no file under crates/ changed; the measurement-only instrumentation leg was reverted before the gates and is retained as a patch in this packet
reason_codes: change 0638 measured the row at 133.61 ms and stated that nothing in that record explained it; this record attributes it

the capture and the commit's recapture are 95.9% of the edit's wall clock, 96.44% of its cycles and 96.08% of its instructions; the working clone, set_shape_text and the publication are the remaining 4%

a marker-stripped control -- the same deck with the MCE namespace URI replaced by an equal-length URI the codec does not recognize, so member count, element count, part-decode count, capture count, fingerprint bytes and uncompressed byte total are all identical -- removes 120.301 ms of 128.123 ms, 93.9%

the mechanism is litchi-pptx asking litchi_ooxml_common::mce to rewrite every slide three times per capture and twice per edit: 94 rewriting passes over 1,726,827 bytes producing 28,064,911 bytes of output, 16.25x amplification, 373,086 namespace re-declarations over 62,181 emitted start tags, 6.00 per element

the complete-package revision proof is NOT the mechanism: package_fingerprint is 0.51% of the capture's native cycles and 0.72% of the whole edit's, about 0.9 ms of 128 ms, so change 0645's design is bounded by that

every candidate that removes the redundant passes either moves when a refusal happens (B, C), needs a public API change and an unanswered bounded-resources question (A), or is change 0588's already-withdrawn design in a crate outside this record's scope (D); nothing is implemented

accepted_evidence.phase_decomposition: probe0649 phases, p50 of 30 samples, three repeats R1/R2/R3, taskset -c 16, over the real deck, the generated corpus shape and the marker-stripped control; the four documented public calls of the edit timed individually
accepted_evidence.aa_floor: widest p50 spread across the three repeats in the same window: 4.31% on the real edit total, 2.89-4.67% on the three phases above 1 ms, 0.67% generated, 0.80% control
accepted_evidence.counts: instrumented leg (twenty-five AtomicU64 counters and one Mutex<Vec<u64>> trace behind twenty-six bump/trace calls in seven files of litchi-ooxml-common and litchi-pptx), differenced across the six prefix stages open/capture/transaction/settext/commit/apply, on all three decks; plus a per-pass input-length trace mapped onto archive member names
accepted_evidence.allocations: the probe's own counting global allocator, per prefix stage, on the real deck and the generated corpus; litchi-perf-baseline-alloc reports no allocation metrics for 0638's ordinary-save family and that gap is recorded
accepted_evidence.cycles_and_instructions: perf stat -e cycles,instructions isolation pairs at N=2 and N=10 differenced over the eight extra iterations, per prefix stage, taskset -c 16
accepted_evidence.native_symbols: perf record -F 999 (dwarf call graph for the capture stage on CPU 16, frame pointers for the whole edit on CPU 17), self-cycle shares
accepted_evidence.instructions_callgrind: callgrind --cache-sim=no --branch-sim=no isolation pair on the capture stage at N=2 and N=6, taskset -c 18; whole-program inclusive Ir per symbol
accepted_evidence.harness_tie_in: change 0638's own pptx_real_file_ordinary_save_* and pptx_ordinary_save_edit selectors run at this base with 0638's harness-only diff (commit 15363b3a8, no file under crates/) applied, 5 warm-ups and 20 samples, taskset -c 16
accepted_evidence.0637_control: change 0637's crate diff (commit 0bf8a8b0e) applied to the base and the count table re-run: every counter identical, so the eager slide-catalog memo does not reach this path

accepted_costs.one_fixture: every number is slide-section-test.pptx on this host at this base; the 16.25x amplification and the 6.00 declarations per element are this deck's, not a producer census
accepted_costs.no_before_after: no production code changed, so the paired structure is real-versus-control and real-versus-generated, not before-versus-after; no claim is registered
accepted_costs.design_ceilings_are_counts: the -62.8%, -43.5% and -62.8% ceilings in the design table are MCE output bytes, which the cycle measurements show this path is linear in, but none of A, B or C is implemented, so none is a measured saving
accepted_costs.callgrind_ranks_work: the per-site inclusive Ir shares (38.95% notes, 27.88% c_sld_name, 27.72% root_name) rank work, not latency; the wall-clock and cycle statements rest on the control and on perf stat
accepted_costs.noisy_sub_millisecond_phases: Snapshot::edit and apply sit on 28.63% and 8.06% floors; their shares are reported to show they are negligible, not to rank them
accepted_costs.control_is_not_a_proposal: the marker-stripped deck is not a semantically valid transformation of a .pptx; it exists inside the measurement and is not retained as a fixture

known_gaps.harness_allocation_metrics: 0638's ordinary-save selector family reports no allocation metrics because the harness-only change that registered it did not reach allocation_metrics.rs; reported, not fixed
known_gaps.producer_census: no census of how many real decks declare the MCE namespace; 43 of 103 members of this one do, carrying 93.0% of its bytes, and 0588 reported 61 of 62 .docx fixtures declaring it in word/document.xml
known_gaps.other_formats: the DOCX and XLSX ordinary-save edits 0638 measured at 0.51 ms and 3.74 ms were not decomposed here; their editors do not run a whole-package capture
known_gaps.third_pass_on_strict_decks: notes::codec::root_conformance runs scan_xml once per conformance in [Transitional, Strict] until one succeeds, so a Strict deck pays the notes pass twice; not measured

withheld: any registered speedup, any before/after delta, any claim that a candidate in the design table would deliver its ceiling, and any statement about decks other than the one fixture

provenance.host: AMD EPYC 9R45, 32 cores, 123 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws, rustc 1.95.0, cargo 1.95.0, valgrind 3.26.0
